title: Estimating qpmR models: priors, posteriors, identification
text: Simulate data known truth, ask posterior find : sampler finds posterior mode first (transformed, unconstrained space), seeds adaptive random-walk Metropolis inverse Hessian, reports split R-hat effective sample sizes. learned column compares posterior prior spread – cheap identification signal. Draws violate Blanchard-Kahn get zero weight, usual truncation prior determinacy region.  Point estimates feed straight back workflow: posterior_forecast() produces fans integrate posterior – draw re-solves model re-filters data, bands combine shock parameter uncertainty:
code: m0 <- qpm_model(variables = vars(x = "x"), shocks = shocks(e),                 equations = eqs(x ~ rho * x[-1] + e),                 params = list(rho = 0.5)) m_true <- qpm_calibrate(m0, rho = 0.8, sigma = c(e = 1.5)) obs <- simulate(qpm_solve(m_true), nsim = 250, seed = 4)  est <- qpm_estimate(m0, obs, pr, iter = 800, chains = 2, seed = 5,                     verbose = FALSE) est #> <qpm_estimate> Bayesian (adaptive RWM) - 2 parameters, 2 chains x 800 draws (burn 400, acceptance 0.28) #>   log-posterior at mode: -444.29 #>   param      prior                  mode     mean       5%      95%  R-hat    ESS learned #>   rho        beta(0.5, 0.2)        0.750    0.745    0.688    0.800   1.02    102 yes #>   e          invgamma(1, 0.5)      1.413    1.418    1.334    1.518   1.02    108 yes #>   'learned' compares posterior to prior sd (yes < 0.5 < some < 0.9 < little) plot(est) m_hat <- apply_estimate(est, "mean") round(coef(est, "mean"), 3) #>   rho     e  #> 0.745 1.418 fc <- posterior_forecast(est, horizon = 10, ndraws = 80) plot(fc, vars = "x")

code: m_bad <- qpm_model(variables = vars(x = "x"), shocks = shocks(e),                    equations = eqs(x ~ a * b * x[-1] + e),                    params = list(a = 0.6, b = 0.9)) qpm_identify(m_bad, params = c("a", "b")) #> <qpm_identification> 2 parameters, observables: x #>   x solution level: rank 1 < 2 - parameters not separately identified #>       combinations involved: a, b #>   ! solution level: near-collinear pairs (only jointly identified): a ~ b (1.000) #>   x moment level (means + autocovariances to lag 3): rank 1 < 2 - parameters not separately identified #>       combinations involved: b, a #>   ! moment level (means + autocovariances to lag 3): near-collinear pairs (only jointly identified): a ~ b (1.000) qpm_identify(qpm_template("bkl"),              params = c("b1", "b2", "b3", "c1", "c2", "a1", "a3"),              observables = c("pi", "i", "q", "y_gap", "dy_obs")) #> <qpm_identification> 7 parameters, observables: pi, i, q, y_gap, dy_obs #>   v solution level: full rank (7), smallest/largest singular value 0.045 #>   v moment level (means + autocovariances to lag 3): full rank (7), smallest/largest singular value 0.023

Food 30-50 percent basket across sub-Saharan Africa South Asia, single-inflation model represent policy question – supply shocks food dominate headline, policy look relative-price component:  Food inflation jumps, headline follows scaled basket weight, core barely moves – policy response stays small. model saying good desk say. Whatever country team changes, qpm_diff() makes reviewable:
